rows: The technical note was published on 4 June 2026.
The release applies to England and Wales; separate routes exist for Scotland and Northern Ireland.
BDUK says the release is optimised for technical users and may exceed spreadsheet display limits.
BDUK plans updated releases alongside OMR closure notices, approximately once every four months.
The release contains BDUK's current view of OMR determinations, current gigabit and future gigabit plans.
The release is not a comprehensive history of delivery through GIS, vouchers, Gigahubs or Superfast.
The premises base uses the latest AddressBase Premium epoch available at the OMR reference point.
Non-postal and demolished premises are filtered from the BDUK premises base.
A missing UPRN may be demolished, derelict or a new build absent from the AddressBase epoch; absence is not a coverage result.
The release is split into 318 English and Welsh local-authority files, with a sample capped at 1,000 rows.
current_gigabit represents BDUK's OMR and own-delivery view, not an independently measured line speed.
future_gigabit records future plans and must not be treated as current availability.
Gigabit White means no qualifying gigabit infrastructure is present and none is likely within three years.
Gigabit Grey/Black can include current infrastructure or planned qualifying infrastructure within three years.
Under Review can reflect unverified claimed current coverage or planned delivery with residual evidence risk.
Initial, Deferred and In Procurement scopes are distinct and cannot be collapsed into delivered coverage.
The GIS final coverage date is the final payment date for initial scope and may change; it is not a premise activation timestamp.
Approved voucher project inclusion is not contractual and does not guarantee delivery to every included premise.
Gigahubs can be descoped and moved to another intervention; scope does not prove a live service.
BDUK reports about 3.7% of intervention premises are in more than one intervention.
Supplier names may vary across subsidiaries, mergers and historical naming, so entity normalisation is required.
Geography assignment uses NSUL first, then postcode NSPL or UPRN ONSUD fallbacks when required.
BDUK says UPRN validity and subsidised-network technical standards are checked through automated and manual assurance.
Around 4,900 GIS contract premises are absent because OS now categorises them as demolished.
current_gigabit can miss delivery after the January 2026 OMR reference date and has supplier-response gaps.
BDUK identifies premises-base, supplier-response/evaluation and reference-date differences from Ofcom PND data.
The July contract-level publication was updated on 20 July 2026.
The table is a snapshot of BDUK management information held on 16 July 2026.
BDUK publishes this contract-level progress series monthly.
The table includes initial-scope contracted premises; deferred scope may be absent.
Deferred-scope premises are not necessarily represented in the contracted total.
CO labels denote Type C Call Off contracts.
The management-information figures are not directly comparable to BDUK official statistics.
Built contracted premises track premises to which the supplier reports delivering gigabit-capable connection.
Official statistics instead report premises connected as a result of BDUK subsidy.
Contract signature or delivery and BDUK ingestion can have a variable time lag.
BDUK says these figures should not be used to assess contractual milestone compliance.
The contract table is rounded to the nearest ten and totals may not sum exactly.
The July table reports 838,490 initial-scope contracted premises.
The July table reports 287,510 built contracted premises.
287,510 divided by 838,490 is about 34.29%; this derived contract ratio is not parcel coverage.
Central Cornwall is listed with 6,940 contracted and 6,940 built premises.
Durham is listed with 4,440 contracted and 4,440 built premises.
Northumberland is listed with 3,830 contracted and 3,830 built premises.
South West Cornwall is listed with 6,400 contracted and 6,400 built premises.
CO8 Cheshire is listed with 18,460 contracted and zero built premises in the snapshot.
Cumbria is listed with 53,540 contracted and 35,040 built premises.
Suffolk is listed with 38,350 contracted and 18,560 built premises.
Lincolnshire and East Riding is listed with 46,970 contracted and 21,840 built premises.
Contract-level counts do not identify the exact coverage state of a selected parcel.
The publication reports contract delivery counts, not measured download or upload speed.
The 16 July snapshot is not a real-time network-availability feed.
The consumer guide was published on 21 November 2022.
The code requires clear speed information when a broadband service is sold.
If a provider-network problem cannot be fixed within 30 days, covered customers must be offered penalty-free exit.
The listed protections apply to providers participating in the code, not automatically to every retail provider.
Providers should give a personalised minimum guaranteed speed.
For superfast products, the guarantee is based on capability of the line entering the premises.
Ofcom recommends ethernet-connected testing for the most accurate consumer speed test.
Wi-Fi can slow the signal and confound a measured speed test.
